# Task brief: <change>

Use this for substantive changes in an existing issue or project plan. Keep
agreed requirements here; a glossary defines terms and an ADR explains an
architectural tradeoff. Resolved decisions belong in these documents, while
raw session history and command logs stay outside version control.

## Outcome

<The observable result the user wants.>

## Scope and authorization

<The owning repository, affected components, boundaries, and operations
already authorized. Identify any additional decision needed before proceeding.>

## Acceptance criteria

- <Observable behavior, including relevant failure or cancellation cases.>

## Verification

<The commands or observations that establish each criterion. Distinguish
fixture tests from machine diagnostics and live activation.>

## Open questions

<Unresolved decisions that block implementation, or "None". Read available
code and documentation before asking the user for facts.>

## Completion evidence

<For each acceptance criterion, report PASS, FAIL, or NOT VERIFIED with a
file reference or actual check result. A reviewer should compare the original
criteria with the changes and evidence, including untracked files.>
